query: How can we reduce declined expense submissions?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: The type of asset being expensed is not directly settable by the actor at submission time (it depends on what is being purchased), so it acts more as a common context/confounder that influences both what gets submitted and whether it is declined. Not named in the query.

per_column.name: submission_context_pattern
per_column.rationale: How a submission is created (automatically generated, manually submitted, system imported, acquisition purchase) is an intervenable lever -- an organization could change or standardize the submission channel/process to reduce declines.

per_column.name: department_group
per_column.rationale: Department is a common cause: it influences both submission behavior/patterns and decline rates, but it is largely a fixed organizational attribute rather than a lever to reduce declines. Note department already exists in the original table, so this is a re-grouping, not truly new information. Not named in the query.

per_column.name: submission_completeness_signal
per_column.rationale: Whether a submission is complete is directly actionable -- submitters/policies can require complete information, making this a settable intervention plausibly reducing declines.

per_column.name: travel_expense_indicator
per_column.rationale: A binary flag largely derivable from category; it is a fixed attribute of the expense (whether it is travel), not an intervenable lever nor a clear common cause. Mostly a descriptive attribute.

per_column.name: description_specificity_level
per_column.rationale: How specific the description is (specific model/brand vs generic vs templated) is something a submitter can control/improve, making it an intervenable lever plausibly affecting declines.

judge.rationale: The query asks how to REDUCE declined submissions, which is a genuine interventional/what-if intent. The added columns do include several intervenable treatments (submission channel/pattern, completeness, description specificity) that an actor could actually set or change to move the outcome, satisfying part (a). However, the confounder structure is weak. Only two columns plausibly act as confounders (asset_category_type, department_group), and department_group merely re-buckets an already-present original column rather than surfacing new common causes. Several added columns are descriptive attributes rather than adjusted-for common causes, and there is no explicit adjustment for classic confounders like submission amount, submitter experience/history, or policy compliance that jointly drive both the levers and declines. So the set sets up plausible interventions but only partially realizes the confounder-adjustment requirement of the what-if claim.
